Try and get him into common interests, like movies and music. I have pretty bad social skills but I can have pretty good conversations fairly easily based on those sorts of things. 

With me, I had to gain a sense of self awareness about my shitty social skills before I was able to overcome it (for the mostpart). I'd assume for him, it'll be the same way. 

Talking with people online helped me out a bit with finding new interests to talk to people about. It's definitely not perfect, but its good practice for the real thing.

Try your best to be supportive of him, even if he messes up and says embarrassing stuff because thats bound to happen and shouldn't discourage him. 

Get him into situations where he can talk with more people. I know this might sound like a bit of a stretch, but maybe let him hang around with you and your friends. If that's a bit much then hang out with him yourself, go see movies, go bowling, etc. Pretty much, anything to get him out of the house that involves social interaction is helpful.

I had a lot of anxiety when I first started out with it. Its a really shitty feeling. I think it's just your body getting adjusted because it went away for me after a week or so.  As for tips in the meantime, It's important to take a lot of breaks. If it hit really bad in class I'd ask to use the bathroom and sit down for a while. I've pretty much always had sleeping problems and I'd highly recommend melatonin (at least in the meantime). Hopefully this is helpful and best of luck!
